defs.def: a person who catches fish, either as a job or as a sport 渔民；钓鱼的人

ex.s: Fishermen go out to sea daily and sell their fish in harbor-side markets.
ex.t: 渔民每天出海，在港区市场售卖他们的鱼。

ex.s: His novel The Old Man and the Sea, about the three-day epic struggle between an elderly fisherman and the biggest fish he had ever caught, won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1953.
ex.t: 他的小说《老人与海》讲述了一位老渔夫与他捕到的最大的鱼之间为期三天的史诗般的搏斗，于1953年获得普利策小说奖。

ex.s: The Old Man and the Sea After 84 days without catching a single fish, an old fisherman, Santiago, sails far out to sea without his devoted apprentice, Manolin.
ex.t: 《老人与海》：84天没有捕到一条鱼后，老渔夫圣地亚哥独自驾船远航出海，没有他忠诚的徒弟马诺林陪伴。

ex.s: Had a late lunch at Fisherman’s Wharf, the district where Italian fishermen first came to San Francisco and set up the fishing industry.
ex.t: 在渔人码头吃了顿迟到的午餐，那是意大利渔民最初来到旧金山并建立渔业的地区。

ex.s: Did so much exploring at Fisherman’s Wharf.
ex.t: 在渔人码头探索了那么多。

ex.s: He is extremely good at describing the adventures of tough men who he believes “can be destroyed but not defeated'" The Old Man and the Sea, one of his most important novels, tells the story of a fisherman named Santiago.
ex.t: 他极擅长描写硬汉的冒险，他相信他们"可以被毁灭但不可以被打败"。《老人与海》是他最重要的小说之一，讲述了一个名叫圣地亚哥的渔夫的故事。
